Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the time to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

- Data residency & GDPR: We support region-specific hosting and have data processing addendum language ready; happy to share our standard DPA.

- Vendor security questionnaire: We can start the questionnaire handoff — attaching a short SOC 2 summary and a vendor-SQ template for your team to populate.
- Compliance roadmap (ask): Marissa will share a short roadmap mapping ISO 27001 and potential SOC scope expansion and timelines (we discussed FedRAMP as a longer-term ask).

Next steps I propose: 
1) Jordan / security team: send back the vendor questionnaire (Vendor-SQ-EnterpriseCorp.xlsx) or highlight any high-priority controls by EOW (Apr 16).
2) Redwood: Marissa to send compliance roadmap + timeline (ISO 27001, SOC scope expansion, FedRAMP feasibility) by Mon Apr 12.
3) Rishi: Happy to schedule a technical deep-dive on encryption/KMS if needed.

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf (PDF, 760 KB), Vendor-SQ-EnterpriseCorp.xlsx (XLSX, 120 KB)

Appreciate the partnership — let us know any immediate blockers.

Subject: Compliance roadmap: ISO 27001, SOC scope expansion, FedRAMP feasibility (EnterpriseCorp)

Hi Jordan & Lauren —

Per Lauren's note, attached is a short draft roadmap that maps our current posture to the certifications you asked about and recommended next steps for EnterpriseCorp's evaluation. High-level summary below: 

- Current posture (Q2 2027): SOC 2 Type II audit in final phase for core hosted control plane; encryption at-rest/in-transit with customer KMS options for Private; DPA template and standard privacy controls in place.

- ISO 27001: We have an internal ISMS in design stage. For an official certification we estimate a 9–12 month program to readiness + external audit, assuming prioritized allocation. This would be prioritized if you require ISO as a procurement condition.

- SOC scope expansion: We can scope Dedicated/Private deployments into SOC workstreams; typical lead time to include those environments in the next audit cycle is ~3–6 months depending on evidence readiness and control mapping.

- FedRAMP: Feasibility is dependent on product segmentation and control maturity. Initial readiness assessment: 6–8 weeks; overall timeline to authorization is typically 12–24 months and requires significant evidence collection and continuous monitoring support.

Recommended immediate next steps for EnterpriseCorp: 
1) Complete the vendor questionnaire and flag must-have controls.
2) If ISO or FedRAMP are procurement gating items, indicate prioritization so we can resource a readiness track.
3) We can provide redacted BAAs and audit artifacts under NDA; please advise if you want those today.

Attachments: Compliance-roadmap-draft.pdf (PDF, 420 KB)
Shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d5e6f (controls matrix, SOC2 evidence index)

If helpful, I'll schedule a 30-minute intake with our Compliance lead + Rishi to walk through any highlighted controls next week. Suggested times: Tue Apr 13 10:00–11:00 or Wed Apr 14 14:00–15:00 (PDT).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Compliance & Trust | Redwood Inference
